pillar_reactions.evidence: Understood the one-session-covers-everything structure and accepted the time efficiency, then asked a run of practical mechanics questions rather than reacting to the value: 'would I run after these workouts or before them?', 'the biggest question is, like, where do I start in terms of, like, the kettlebell I need, right? Like, which one?' and an earlier 'knowing which ones to buy when I'm up there next week'. He also volunteered the one feature he actually wanted — 'I love the component of videoing my form, right?... that's how I've been injured in the past.' The rep deferred the running question to Trevor ('I don't want to recommend that right now') but answered the bell size himself with 16kg.

Agreed with the what/when/how-much frame and pre-empted most of it himself — 'I know the answer for, like, eating out, you know, it's like fish, and chicken, or steak, and no, you know, potatoes, or fried food' and 'I know most of the right answers. It's just actually doing it.' Already runs intermittent fasting in roughly an 11-to-7 window and says he responds well to it. No questions and no pushback; he treated nutrition as solved knowledge and unsolved behaviour, which is exactly the bridge the rep then used into accountability.

The only enthusiastic pillar reaction in the batch, and he volunteered it before the rep got there — 'I think the accountability part is really big for me', 'Like, I want that. I need somebody being like, no, this is what we need to do', and after delivery 'I think knowing somebody will be there to put me, like, you know, hold my feet to the fire, so to speak, is really helpful.' He tied it directly to his own failure mode: 'life gets in the way. I'm busy. And then I, you know, I have tons of excuses.' This pillar sold the programme; the other two were hygiene.

anchors.raw: So what was the $1.99 a month that I have already paid? What was that for?
anchors.note: Almost certainly $199/month for the Primal University Skool community, which he had already bought before this call; the transcript renders it as $1.99. The rep separated it cleanly — 'That's a school thing. That's a primal university, but that's not coaching with Trevor.' Worth noting for the rollup that a paying low-tier subscriber was upsold to the $6,000 programme, and that the two products were briefly confused in the buyer's head at the moment of purchase.

anchors.raw: I've been training with a trainer, but that's going to end at the end of this month. And I'm just looking for something to now go to and still continue getting back in shape
anchors.note: An in-person New York personal trainer was already in the budget and is expiring exactly as this decision is made. The strongest supportive anchor available and the rep never priced against it — he never asked what the trainer cost, which would have made $1,000/month look cheap rather than requiring a split.

anchors.raw: for the last four months, I've been doing, I've been microdosing GLP-1s, and I found I've gotten zero results
anchors.note: Alongside NAD+ injections every two to three days, Viome blood/stool/urine analysis with bespoke supplements, a Whoop, a Hume body-composition scale and a large supplement stack. Substantial and ongoing discretionary health spend with self-reported zero return — the ideal setup for a value reframe that was never made.

anchors.raw: I work completely on commission. I don't have a salary. So one month I make $100,000, one month I make $2,000.
anchors.note: Not an affordability problem but a timing one, and the only thing standing between this call and a paid-in-full close. He said outright he would pay in full if it saved money — 'if it's easier, and if I save money by paying you $6,000 upfront, fine' — and the rep never took him up on it, instead volunteering the split.

unmet_demand.want: Someone to take charge of his supplement stack, bloodwork and peptide regimen — he asked directly whether to stop the GLP-1, whether to look into TRT, and what to take instead
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme does not include clinical or dietetic oversight. The rep said so explicitly and told him to source it himself — 'it has to be a clinical dietitian, and do some research. Maybe someone from your close circle is using one.' The prospect is in the market for exactly this, is already paying for Viome and NAD+, and is currently using ChatGPT as the substitute.

unmet_demand.want: Running kept in the programme and sequenced properly around the kettlebell sessions, three to five times a week
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Nothing says the programme cannot do it and the rep implied it can — 'if you enjoy that, he will keep that... he will incorporate that into the daily schedule' — but he then refused to answer the actual question and pushed it to Trevor. The prospect asked twice and left without an answer on something he called life-saving: 'Totally. Saved my life. Running.'

unmet_demand.want: Assurance that loaded kettlebell work is safe for him given an unexplained three-day paralysis, ongoing left-side weakness and prior shoulder surgery
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Never addressed by anyone. The prospect raised the risk himself and self-managed it — 'for me, it's going to be like starting out like light, right? Like not pushing myself' — and the rep answered with a strength goal and a 16kg starting bell rather than a clearance step. There is no clinical screening layer in the offer to satisfy this demand.
